sentences.en: The brief pause in the Iran war appears to be over the U.S. resuming strikes against Iran as the war now expands to Egypt.
sentences.cn: 伊朗战争中的短暂停火似乎已经结束，美国恢复对伊朗的打击，战争现已扩大到埃及。
sentences.structure: 主句 + 伴随状语（as从句）
sentences.analysis: 主句为'The brief pause... appears to be over'，后接动名词短语'resuming strikes'作伴随状语，'as'引导时间状语从句说明战争扩大。

sentences.en: Video from Iran's state media claims to show the aftermath of one of those strikes on an island in the Strait of Hormuz, claiming that missiles fell there in a residential neighborhood.
sentences.cn: 伊朗国家媒体的视频声称展示了其中一次打击的后果，打击发生在霍尔木兹海峡的一个岛屿上，声称导弹落在了一个居民区。
sentences.structure: 主句 + 现在分词短语（claiming that...）
sentences.analysis: 主句为'Video... claims to show...'，后接现在分词短语'claiming that...'作补充说明，其中'that'引导宾语从句。

sentences.en: And when we talk about the broadening of this war, Erica, and it's important to note, Saudi Arabia has been impacted by Iran's proxy network, not only the Iranian backed Iraqi militants in Iraq, but also the Yemeni Houthis.
sentences.cn: 当我们谈到这场战争的扩大时，埃里卡，重要的是要注意，沙特阿拉伯一直受到伊朗代理人网络的影响，不仅包括伊拉克境内伊朗支持的伊拉克武装分子，还包括也门胡塞武装。
sentences.structure: 时间状语从句 + 主句（并列结构）
sentences.analysis: 'when'引导时间状语从句，主句为'it's important to note...'，后接'not only... but also...'并列结构说明影响来源。

sentences.en: And there's concern that there could be sort of a bigger drawing of other actors into this war.
sentences.cn: 人们担心可能会有更多其他行为体被卷入这场战争。
sentences.analysis: 主句为'There's concern'，后接'that'引导的同位语从句说明担心的内容。

sentences.en: Republican Senator John Cornyn of Texas still refusing to support Todd Blanche as attorney general, forcing Republican leaders in the Senate to postpone a vote to advance his nomination.
sentences.cn: 得克萨斯州共和党参议员约翰·科宁仍然拒绝支持托德·布兰奇担任司法部长，迫使参议院共和党领导人推迟推进其提名的投票。
sentences.structure: 独立主格结构 + 现在分词短语（forcing...）
sentences.analysis: 前半部分为独立主格结构'Republican Senator... refusing...'，后半部分'forcing...'为现在分词短语作结果状语。

sentences.en: And it's not a big ask.
sentences.analysis: 主语'it'指代前文提到的要求，'not a big ask'为固定表达，意为'不过分的要求'。

sentences.en: But to put sort of the focus on why is it that Republicans themselves aren't going to let him get through this process, to officially become an A.G. I think underscores all of the negative aspects going into the midterm elections for Republicans, and especially Todd Blanche, when I believe most people don't think that he is in there to do the best job for the American people or for the Department of Justice, even, but that he's there to do the best that he can do for Donald Trump himself.
sentences.cn: 但是，把焦点放在为什么共和党人自己不会让他通过这一程序正式成为司法部长上，我认为这凸显了共和党进入中期选举的所有负面因素，尤其是托德·布兰奇，因为我相信大多数人认为他并不是为了美国人民或司法部的最佳利益而任职，而是为了尽最大努力为唐纳德·特朗普本人服务。
sentences.structure: 不定式短语作主语 + 主句（I think）+ 宾语从句（underscores...）+ 时间状语从句（when...）
sentences.analysis: 句首'But to put...'为不定式短语作主语，主句为'I think'，后接省略'that'的宾语从句'underscores...'，其中包含'when'引导的时间状语从句，该从句中又包含'that'引导的宾语从句。

sentences.en: I almost think that Senator Cornyn is surprised that this relatively simple request hasn't yet been met.
sentences.cn: 我几乎认为科宁参议员对这样一个相对简单的请求尚未得到满足感到惊讶。
sentences.structure: 主句 + 宾语从句（that...）+ 形容词从句（that...）
sentences.analysis: 主句为'I almost think'，后接'that'引导的宾语从句，其中又包含'that'引导的形容词从句说明'is surprised'的原因。

sentences.en: And the message is essentially talk about the economy, which not surprising.
sentences.cn: 信息本质上是谈论经济，这并不令人意外。
sentences.structure: 主句 + 非限制性定语从句
sentences.analysis: 主句为'The message is... talk about the economy'，后接'which'引导的非限制性定语从句修饰整个主句。

sentences.en: But the Democratic Party doesn't always do a terrific job of this, they often end up talking about social issues that are wedge issues that are very important to the Democratic base, but less important to these swing voters and working class voters who are like, you know, I can't think about the end of the world, I need to think about the end of the month as the report phrased it.
sentences.cn: 但民主党并不总是做得很好，他们最终往往谈论的是社会问题，这些问题是分裂性问题，对民主党基本盘非常重要，但对这些摇摆选民和工薪阶层选民来说不那么重要，他们就像报告所说的那样：'我不能考虑世界末日，我需要考虑月底。'
sentences.structure: 并列句 + 定语从句（that...）+ 定语从句（who...）
sentences.analysis: 两个并列句由'but'连接，第二个分句中包含'that'引导的定语从句修饰'social issues'，该从句中又包含'who'引导的定语从句修饰'swing voters and working class voters'。

topics.title: 美国对伊朗军事行动
topics.content: 美国对伊朗发动新一轮大规模打击，战争扩大至埃及、约旦、科威特等地。伊朗通过代理人网络（如伊拉克武装分子、也门胡塞武装）进行报复，沙特阿拉伯也受到影响。局势升级引发对地区冲突扩大的担忧。
topics.keywords: Iran, strikes, proxy network, escalation, Middle East

topics.title: 美国中期选举与民意
topics.content: CNN最新民调显示民主党在中期选举中领先共和党8个百分点，民主党选民热情更高。但选民仍对生活成本问题不满，认为两党关注不足。民主党需聚焦经济议题以争取工薪阶层选民，而共和党内部存在分歧，如科宁参议员抵制布兰奇提名。
topics.keywords: midterms, CNN poll, Democrats, Republicans, economy, working class

topics.title: 托德·布兰奇司法部长提名受阻
topics.content: 参议员科宁因布兰奇拒绝书面承诺废除反武器化基金而推迟投票，布兰奇提名陷入危险。科宁此前在初选中被特朗普击败，此举被视为个人报复。布兰奇曾为特朗普律师，其独立性受质疑。
topics.keywords: Todd Blanche, Attorney General, nomination, John Cornyn, anti-weaponization fund

U.S. Launches "Heavy Wave Of Strikes" Against Iranian Targets; GOP Holdouts Postpone Vote On Blanche Nomination; CNN Poll: Voters Favor Democrats Heading Into The Midterms. Aired 6-6:30a ET

Aired July 30, 2026 - 06:00   ET

THIS IS A RUSH TRANSCRIPT. THIS COPY MAY NOT BE IN ITS FINAL FORM AND MAY BE UPDATED.

ERICA HILL, CNN ANCHOR: This just in to CNN -- new CNN polling shows Democrats now leading Republicans in the midterms. So what's behind the surge?

SEN. BERNIE SANDERS (I-VT): That people are saying, you know what status quo policies no longer are good enough. We want a government that works for all of us.

HILL: The brief pause in the Iran war appears to be over the U.S. resuming strikes against Iran as the war now expands to Egypt.

A Senate hearing on COVID quickly turning confrontational. Why were the attacks on Dr. Fauci so personal?

SEN. BERNIE MORENO (R-OH): Who the (EXPLETIVE DELETED) do you think you were for doing that?

HILL: President Trump's pick for attorney general hits a roadblock, and the resistance coming from Republicans

MANU RAJU, CNN CHIEF CONGRESSIONAL CORRESPONDENT: Why do you think they're not getting the message from you?

SEN. JOHN CORNYN (R-TX): Maybe they think they can roll me.

(BEGIN VIDEO CLIP) DONALD TRUMP, PRESIDENT OF THE UNITED STATESE: We're going to be hitting them very hard because it's our turn to hit them. They know what's coming. They're asking us not to do it, but they nevertheless took a shot. So, it's our turn

HILL: The U.S. military unleashing new attacks on Iran, making good on that promise. Good morning, everyone. I'm Erica Hill in for Audie Cornish.

We begin with the new strikes overnight, a new video in from U.S. Central Command, which shows what the military is calling a heavy wave of strikes aimed at Iranian equipment, command posts and southern coastal defense sites. Video from Iran's state media claims to show the aftermath of one of those strikes on an island in the Strait of Hormuz, claiming that missiles fell there in a residential neighborhood.

CNN's Eleni Giokos joining us now from Dubai.

So, in terms of this latest rounds of strikes, Eleni, what more do we know about the strikes? And also, the response at this hour from Iran?

ELENI GIOKOS, CNN BUSINESS CORRESPONDENT: Well, as you say, President Trump making good on those threats yesterday, in fact, using very harsh language to emphasize how hard they were going to strike Iran. CENTCOM confirming those strikes, and Iranian state media saying that they heard blasts across southern Iran.

Importantly, Bandar Abbas, that important port city. We heard about blasts heard on Kish as well as Khuzestan province, which borders Iraq. Now, in Qeshm Island, Iranian state media releasing footage showing rubble rescue operations there, saying that a strike had impacted a residential building. Multiple injuries reported there as well.

Now, in retaliation today, just this morning, Iran targeted Jordan once again. Five missiles were intercepted and then Kuwait confirming that there was a deadly attack targeting a Chinese company in the northern part of the country. One person died and there was extensive damage there as well.

And when we talk about the broadening of this war, Erica, and it's important to note, Saudi Arabia has been impacted by Iran's proxy network, not only the Iranian backed Iraqi militants in Iraq, but also the Yemeni Houthis. And what we've been seeing here is another further issue, where two vessels are off the coast of Egypt. The port had been impacted by a drone.

Now, no group has claimed responsibility for this strike. But there is continued concern that were climbing this escalation ladder, how President Trump is going to respond to these new attacks on Jordan and Kuwait, and importantly, what the positioning is of the proxy network. Saudi Arabia, in meetings with J.D. Vance as well as President Trump yesterday was talking about how they want deescalation, but also have a right to protect themselves.

And they even struck targets in eastern Iraq in a joint operation with CENTCOM earlier this week. And there's concern that there could be sort of a bigger drawing of other actors into this war.

HILL: Yeah. Certainly, the stakes shifting every day. And as we look at this, certainly ramping up. Eleni, appreciate it. Thank you.

Just ahead here on CNN THIS MORNING, the weapons warning as the stockpile dwindles in the U.S. as the war with Iran making America more vulnerable.

Plus, heavy rain and rescues. This morning, the cleanup underway after flash floods across the northeast.

And a Senate panel will not vote today on Todd Blanche's nomination as A.G. Is this one Republican's revenge for the president primarying him?

The group chat has some thoughts.

RAJU: Why do you think they're not getting the message from you?

CORNYN: Maybe they think they can roll me.

RAJU: Can they roll?

HILL: Republican Senator John Cornyn of Texas still refusing to support Todd Blanche as attorney general, forcing Republican leaders in the Senate to postpone a vote to advance his nomination. And that throws Blanche nomination into serious jeopardy. Now, just days before the Senate breaks for its long August recess, Cornyn showing no sign of backing down in his battle with the Justice Department over its controversial $1.8 billion so-called anti weaponization fund.

CORNYN: He refused to commit to writing what he testified to under oath. And it's not a big ask.

REPORTER: Why don't you think Todd Blanche has met your demands at around the 11th hour before this vote?

CORNYN: Well, I assume he's getting some pushback from the president's lawyers.

HILL: Cornyn, a member of the YOLO caucus, if you will, was primarily by President Trump, of course, lost his seat.

Today in the group chat, Tamara Keith, senior political correspondent at NPR, host of the "NPR Politics" podcast; Terry Schilling, president of the American Principles Project. And Maria Cardona, CNN political commentator and Democratic strategist.

Happy Friday eve to all who celebrate. Nice to have you guys here.

As we look at where things stand as this process dries out, dries out, dries out -- drags out, I should say, Blanche is still acting A.G. in some ways. Is this actually a win for the White House, maria?

MARIA CARDONA, CNN POLITICAL COMMENTATOR: Well, I think you can look at it two ways. Yes, he's acting A.G. and you know, even Democrats say that he could continue in that role. But to put sort of the focus on why is it that Republicans themselves aren't going to let him get through this process, to officially become an A.G. I think underscores all of the negative aspects going into the midterm elections for Republicans, and especially Todd Blanche, when I believe most people don't think that he is in there to do the best job for the American people or for the Department of Justice, even, but that he's there to do the best that he can do for Donald Trump himself.

He used to be his lawyer. He even had a Freudian slip during one of the sessions in Congress when they asked him, are you a lawyer or are you the A.G.? He was like, I'm the president's lawyer, or I was the president's lawyer.

So that does not inspire confidence in him, in his role as the A.G., and especially when it comes to the Epstein files, which I think is just going to be a negative for him.

HILL: Is, is -- Terry, is the president losing his grip on the party?

TERRY SCHILLING, PRESIDENT, AMERICAN PRINCIPLES PROJECT: No, I don't think so. I think if you look at what's happening here, these are two senators that don't have to worry about reelection. Tillis is retiring. John Cornyn just lost a primary battle. I do think this is some personal politics going on.

But I was just going to say Todd Blanche has done an amazing job at protecting parental rights. He has this whole anti-weaponization of government coalition. He just had a bunch of parents in just last month. I was at that meeting, versus Merrick Garland, both Tillis and John Cornyn voted to confirm Merrick Garland, who weaponized the government, who voted for him, or, sorry, who weaponized the government against these parents, classified them as domestic terrorists.

It's really -- really sad to see. We need to be unified as a party. And these guys that don't have to worry about their reelections really are hurting us.

HILL: So, you're saying that it's them not worrying about reelection makes it political, or is it just that they're voting.

SCHILLING: With their personal, personal.

When we -- when we look at how we got to this place, there is a lot of -- as we heard from Senator Cornyn, right? He has this focus on the fund. So Todd Blanche was asked about it. I want to play what Todd Blanche had to say.

TODD BLANCHE, ACTING ATTORNEY GENERAL: We are not moving forward with the fund.

REP. GRACE MENG (D-NY): Not moving forward, ever.

MENG: Would both of you now sign and release documents reversing the DOJ's position on the fund?

BLANCHE: I'm not -- we're not moving forward with the fund. I'm not committing to putting anything in writing. And I said it over and over again.

MENG: Nothing in writing?

BLANCHE: I mean, I don't know what the purpose of putting something in writing. I'm telling you what we're doing. Meaning like, what's the -- why do I need to put something in writing if I'm telling you what we're doing?

HILL: So, to that point, there's a lot of back and forth on the writing. I just want to say, the most recent CNN reporting, a DOJ official told CNN that a written proposal was sent to Cornyn staff on Tuesday, Cornyn told CNN. And I'm quoting him here that it was not clear -- it was clear. Sorry. He was clear. He has not seen, quote, a single piece of writing that is responsive to what I've requested.

How did this, in particular become the sticking point?

TAMARA KEITH, SENIOR POLITICAL CORRESPONDENT, AXIOS: Oh, because this was announced just as all of this was coming as his nomination was coming. And it, you know, it was it was actually part of Todd Blanche's efforts to get the job to win over the president, to say that he should be the permanent attorney general, along with some prosecutions and other things that that are very in line with what President Trump made clear that he wanted. I almost think that Senator Cornyn is surprised that this relatively simple request hasn't yet been met. My sense is that Senator Cornyn wants to vote this through. He has

been a good Republican senator for a very long time and doesn't totally relish being in the YOLO caucus. And yet, this is sort of just hanging out there for now.

CARDONA: But can I just say this underscores the lack of credibility for Todd Blanche people say, if we can really trust you to say or to believe that this is not happening, put it in writing. But clearly, we know that the president doesn't want him to put it in writing because the president wants this. So, the American people, again, are left with, we can't trust these people.

KEITH: At least one judge has asked for it in writing, too.

HILL: Yeah. So, we'll see. We'll see if it ever materializes.

As we wait, we do want to take a look ahead here on CNN THIS MORNING.

It's some new polling which shows that advantage I mentioned at the top of the show for Democrats heading into the midterms. The question, of course, can they actually turn that into votes when the time comes?

Plus, fire crews in France today could finally see some much needed relief as the weather turns.

And good morning to our friends joining us from Charlotte. Pretty sunrise you have coming up here, 6:15 a.m., for sunrise over the city.

UNIDENTIFIED FEMALE: I wanted to hear from myself him explain why Congress has lost their backbone.

UNIDENTIFIED MALE: People are pissed and. And frankly, I am too.

HILL: There you go. People are pissed. Voters across the U.S. are angry. They're frustrated.

And this morning, new CNN polling may also offer a bit of a red flag for Republicans heading into the midterms. This new polling for CNN shows a possible Democratic surge.
